findings.body: EpicReconcilerWorkflow is bound (cloudflare/wrangler.toml:291-294) but nothing under cloudflare/src calls EPIC_RECONCILER.create; runs.ts:244/606 still start RUN_WORKFLOW, which boots a container agent (run-workflow.ts:1430). No deployed run is driven by the new reconciler, so the Phase 4 gate cannot be performed.
findings.title: Wire the run route to EpicReconcilerWorkflow; today only tests create it

findings.body: epic-reconciler.ts has no CI wait, no hold on red naming the job, no refusal on absent CI, and posts neither verdict nor findings on the PR; a closeout job reporting done is closed like an implement tick (:455). The Go admitCloseout (internal/reconcile/dispatch.go:306) has no TypeScript counterpart, so the epic's gated hand-over cannot happen on the Cloudflare host.
findings.title: Port the CI-gated close-out and PR-posted review to the Workflow reconciler

findings.body: epic-reconciler.ts:717-799 records the attempt marker before executor.start and merges start's sandbox/process_id/branch/base_sha only in memory (:798). Every later pass, and every restart, calls namedSandbox(binding, undefined)/getProcess(undefined) (sandbox-executor.ts:312-314). FakeExecutor keys on job_id, which hides it.
findings.title: Workflow reconciler never persists the sandbox handle, so no real attempt can be re-inspected

findings.body: sandbox-executor.ts:533 calls issueRunToken per boot, which revokes all live tokens for the run_id (gateway.ts:309). With max_parallel > 1 the second start cuts the first worker off with 403 run_token_revoked; adopt (:255) and cancel (:417) do the same. run-workflow.ts:2615-2620 documents and avoids this hazard; the tests stub boot.
findings.title: SandboxExecutor boot revokes every sibling worker's gateway token in the run

findings.body: epic-reconciler.ts:916,961-1013 puts the renewed/re-acquired token in a local but updates holder, which the contents store reads, only after the step returns. After a lapse every write is refused not_holder, the retry renews with the old token and gets lease_lost, and the run fails.
findings.title: A re-acquired publish slot token is not used for that pass's writes, so a lease lapse ends the run

findings.body: cloudflare/wrangler.toml orders migrations v1, v4, v2, v3 (lines 23/38/64/68). Wrangler applies entries after the last deployed tag, so an existing deployment at v3 never creates RepoRoom and the REPO_ROOMS binding fails at deploy. Move the v4 block after v3 and add an ordering test.
findings.title: RepoRoom migration v4 is listed before v2/v3 in wrangler.toml

findings.body: sandbox-executor.ts:262,277 uses workerBranch(epic, tick) while the handle records spec.write_ref from writeRefFor(run, tick, attempt). On a redispatch collect counts the previous attempt's commits; the Go side moved to one ref per attempt for exactly this (internal/reconcile/dispatch.go:1100-1109).
findings.title: Cloud worker pushes a per-tick branch, not the attempt's write_ref

findings.body: SandboxAttemptHandle (sandbox-executor.ts:125) is flat with no schema_version/issued_at/nested handle and ~15 extra top-level fields against contracts/job-protocol.json's closed job_handle; status uses running|exited|gone. Records also hard-code source_sha to forty zeros and refs/heads/main (epic-reconciler.ts:741-742,794). No test compares against Go-produced records.
findings.title: Cloud attempt records do not match the job_handle contract or local provenance

findings.body: rfc3339 uses toISOString (.000Z vs tk's Z) and the test locks it in; encodeTick drops unknown fields; ready lacks tk's limit; next ignores manual/after; close ignores awaiting; claiming an epic is wave-gated; no activity entry. tracker-client.test.ts validates shapes for a hand-picked command list and never iterates manifest.commands, so 'proven against the pinned fixtures' is not yet true.
findings.title: TypeScript tracker client writes bytes tk would not, and its fixture test is hand-picked

findings.body: GateConfig defaults to <repo>/.tick/runners.toml (internal/reconcile/reconcile.go:358), i.e. main. Every ts gate record in epic-ncv ran without `pnpm lint` although epic/ncv's runners.toml carries it, so the epic's TypeScript was never gated by its own config. Decide which config governs, and record the digest of the one used.
findings.title: Integrated gate reads runners.toml from the controller's checkout, not the integrated head

findings.body: closeout.go:213/343 name ciSHA only on green; red/pending branches say 'the head that includes the close-out's own commits' even when the verdict was borrowed (:352/356). closeout_ci.go:108-122 stops at the first ancestor with any state and forge.go:323-331 maps cancelled to pending, which ci.yml's cancel-in-progress produces. No test moves the PR head during a close-out.
findings.title: Close-out CI verdict names its commit only on green, and a cancelled ancestor run parks it

findings.body: Write-grade workers get the operator's unscoped GITHUB_TOKEN (sandbox-executor.ts:548 -> worker-boot.ts:462) and push directly; sweep-dispatch.ts:499 and signal-inbox.ts:1339 call commitTickRecord, which writes .tick/issues/<id>.json, not the disjoint .tick/signals/ that repo-room.ts:48-53 claims. This widens promoted finding b52c827.
findings.title: Repository writes bypass the RepoRoom publisher (worker token, sweep-dispatch, SignalInbox)

findings.body: epic-ncv stopped five times only because a tick reported a finding that needed a person to triage; as designed, a run is unattended only if nothing finds anything. The Phase 4 gate counts one intervention as failure. Choose: carry untriaged findings to the PR (as the epic AC allows for the final review) or keep the hold and say the gate cannot be met.
findings.title: Decide how the untriaged-finding hold coexists with an unattended gate

findings.body: The TS reconciler has no wave barrier or review/closeout hold-back and its claim ignores blocked_by (epic-reconciler.ts:678-804, tracker-client.ts:779-818); the slot is per repository not per epic; a lapsed run may re-acquire and continue. These differ from the Go reconciler and are not recorded as decisions anywhere.
findings.title: Record the Workflow host's reconciler semantics changes as decisions

findings.body: deploy-factory.yml triggers on v* tags and workflow_dispatch with no needs: on CI and no environment protection, so a tag on a red commit, or a dispatch from any unmerged branch, deploys the factory.
findings.title: Gate deploy-factory.yml on green CI and a protected environment

findings.body: ticfac amended its Phase 4 gate on 2026-09-18 so that a person merges. SPEC 12 Phase 4 and w1z A1 still require a merged PR with the laptop offline. Amend the SPEC or record there that ticfac diverges deliberately and why.
findings.title: SPEC 12 Phase 4 / w1z A1 still say 'merged PR'; ticfac's gate now stops at a reviewed, CI-verified PR

response.summary: the review is complete and its verdict is NOT READY. The Phase 4 gate run never happened (epic-ncv ran on local herdr with 13+ interventions), and the Workflow host cannot yet run one (defects 1–7).
